record.paper_title: Some open problems in Banach space theory
record.original_question: Does every infinite-dimensional Banach space X have an infinite-dimensional separable quotient space?

evidence.quote:
(Q.1~) Does every infinitely dimensional- Banach space X have an infinite. dimensio-
naL separable quotient space ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional Banach space over the real or complex field. A quotient space of $X$ is a Banach space of the form $X/M$, where $M$ is a closed linear subspace of $X$, equipped with the quotient norm $\|x+M\| = \inf_{m\in M}\|x+m\|$. A Banach space is said to be separable if it contains a countable dense subset.

Question: Does every infinite-dimensional Banach space $X$ admit a closed subspace $M \subset X$ such that the quotient $X/M$ is both infinite-dimensional and separable?
artifact.status_search_result: The separable quotient problem (often attributed to Banach and Mazur, ca. 1932) remains open in general. Positive answers are known in many special classes—reflexive spaces, weakly compactly generated spaces, dual spaces, and more recent generalizations such as "dual-like" Banach spaces—but the general case has not been resolved. Recent surveys and articles (e.g., 2020 and 2022) continue to describe it as a longstanding open problem.

status_evidence.title: Observations on the Separable Quotient Problem for Banach Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: The longstanding Banach–Mazur separable quotient problem asks whether every infinite-dimensional Banach space has a quotient that is both infinite-dimensional and separable.
status_evidence.claim: Problem is described as longstanding and open, with positive results in special cases.

status_evidence.title: Revisiting Mazur separable quotient problem (1932)
status_evidence.snippet: The centenary of the still open problem of the existence of a separable quotient of infinite dimension in a Banach space will be in 2032.
